title: Crossing the Atlantic with Ellington: Braud's storm and toupee
summary: He likes sea travel; Braud blamed Bigard for talking up a storm when the ship showed a movie called Storm at Daybreak, and later threw his London toupee into the ocean.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How many trips did you make to Europe with Duke?
How many trips did you make to Europe with Duke?
With Duke? About two or three, something like that. I'm quite not sure.
But it's -- I like the boat. You know, I get more fun on the boat than anything else.
There was a lot of music played on the boat, wasn't there?
Yeah, well, we only gave a concert, and when we gave the concert we had the boat for ourselves then, you know, because we went tourist and when you're going tourist

you're only limited to go to certain parts of the boat. But when we gave the concert, we went to all parts of the boat. The first class, second class, tourist, everything, third class. But we had a lot of fun.

I had to laugh the last time we went. Braud -- I was talking to Braud and I said, 'Braud, do you ever' -- because he had been over before, you know. So I said, 'Did you ever get in a storm on your trip?' I was scared. So he says, 'Boy, don't talk like that. Don't talk about storms.' He said, 'You don't want to never see nothing or get into one like that. You just forget that storm business.' And I said, 'Why?' I said, 'Did you have a bad time?' He said, 'You don't know what it's like.'
So that same day on the boat they were showing a movie and the movie was Storm at Daybreak. So I said, 'Hey, Braud, come here. There's a big sign out here, see. 'Storm at Daybreak.'"
He said, 'Damn it. You kept talking. Now you've talked up a storm.' Oh, he was angry with me then. He said, 'You're crazy. I knew this was going to happen.' So I said, 'Man, it's a movie.'
Then he bought a toupee in London. You see, he didn't let anybody know till we was on the boat, you know.
So in the morning we got up and he's got this toupee on but he's got that thing all lopsided, you know. So we had a table, a big table. It was always reserved for us for our food and all.
When he walked into that dining -- I call it dining -- and everybody looked at him and, boy, you never saw such laughing and commotion: He went right out and took the toup and threw it in the ocean.

But I had a lot of fun, though. And Sonny, he stayed stoned all the time. And Duke would never go to bed because he'd always try to con somebody to stay up and gamble, because every time the boat would swerve, he was trembling like that map. (unintelligible).
